twitter.agent: Chinese copper smelters (CSPT, Jiangxi Copper, Tongling)
twitter.content: With the 2026 benchmark settled at $0/t and the SMM imported concentrate index at −$231.68/dmt, there is no economic case for running smelters on concentrate. CSPT members should hold the line on the Q4 maintenance cuts and demand index-linked floors in the 2027 talks. Our refined output is up 4% y/y only because of byproducts — that ends when sulphuric acid outlets stay shut. TCs stay negative into 2027; the squeeze persists.

We settled at $0/t in January because the concentrate market reflected reality: mines are scarce and smelting capacity is not. For 2027 we are firmly behind a drift to index-linked terms — but note ICSG projects 3.1% mine growth next year. If Cobre Panama talks progress and Kamoa delivers 500kt+, TCs recover and the squeeze narrative dies. Supply catches up.

Panama's commission recommended opening negotiations on 30 September. We are ready to restart Cobre Panama — roughly 330kt/yr of contained copper — the single largest swing factor for 2027. Every quarter of delay keeps spot TCs deeply negative and supports prices above $14,000. A restart framework in H1 2027 is achievable if the government moves.

The September accident at El Teniente and a 13% grade decline over four years are not abstract — Chile produced 2.88 Mt Jan–Jul, down 7% y/y. Cochilco's +5.2% rebound forecast for 2027 assumes flawless execution across our project pipeline. History says treat that forecast with skepticism. Structural subtraction supports the deficit-to-price transmission.

Kamoa-Kakula guidance steps to 500,000–540,000 t in 2027 from 380,000–420,000 t, with mining rates at 10 Mt/a — a named +100–120kt increment on stream. Phase 4 ramps toward 2028 and is not in our 2027 numbers. DRC supply is the most reliable part of the bull-case-for-supply; we will hit guidance.

CNIA recommended expanding state copper reserves in February 2026, but buying outright at $14,473/t would run directly against our 2021 auction precedent of countercyclical releases in 20,000–30,000 t batches. If ICSG's 368kt 2027 surplus materializes, expect SRB to absorb opportunistically at dips — not to chase record highs.

Suspended sulphuric acid exports since May 2026 plus the scrap-tax crackdown have tightened both feed streams for CSPT smelters, even as we push electrification demand. Grid, EV and datacenter build-outs keep Chinese copper demand growth positive despite property drag below 2%. The policy mix is deliberately squeezing refined supply — prices stay supported.

The commission recommended negotiations, but we finance an orderly closure in parallel. No scope, timing or legal structure has been set. Any restart must deliver fiscal revenue and political stability first — Cobre Panama volumes should NOT be assumed in 2027 balance sheets. Bear cases relying on our restart are speculative.

twitter.content: CSPT member smelters confirm Q4 maintenance program: seven member smelters will undertake 30–60 day planned maintenance over October–November 2026, with approximately 80,000 tonnes of Q4 refined output taken offline. This coordinated discipline reflects feed scarcity and deeply negative spot TCs, and we enter the 2027 benchmark negotiations at Asia Copper Week seeking terms that restore viability to the custom smelting segment.

Ahead of Asia Copper Week, NDRC and MIIT call on the smelting sector to strengthen industry self-discipline and strictly implement the CSPT output-cut commitment made in November 2025, and to advance capacity replacement in an orderly manner. We will continue to improve the utilization of domestic and imported raw material resources, ensure the security of the industrial chain and supply chain, and promote the high-quality development of the nonferrous metals industry.

First Quantum welcomes the commission's 30 September recommendation and confirms we have formally proposed to the Government of Panama that both parties begin technical working-level discussions on a restart framework, including provisions to fund an orderly, phased closure plan. We remain committed to constructive dialogue; the scope, timing and legal structure of any restart have not been determined and remain subject to approval by the Government of Panama.

Antofagasta confirms it will participate in discussions regarding 2027 benchmark terms during Asia Copper Week in Shanghai, 17–19 November 2026. We note the continued tightness in the global concentrate market and value our long-standing, constructive relationships with Chinese customers. As is our practice, we will not comment on the details of ongoing commercial discussions.

twitter.agent: Chinese copper smelters (CSPT, Jiangxi Copper, Tongling)
twitter.content: With spot TCs at −$231.68/dmt (SMM, 30 Sep 2026) and concentrate imports down 4.1% y/y, our Q4 maintenance plan — including ~80,000 t of scheduled cuts and 30–60 day outages at seven CSPT member smelters — is firm and verifiable in monthly output data. We reaffirm self-discipline: no smelter gains from a race to treat ore below cost.

twitter.agent: Chinese copper smelters (CSPT, Jiangxi Copper, Tongling)

twitter.content: We note CSPT members' Q4 maintenance program as a concrete step toward self-discipline and orderly market supply, consistent with the November 2025 >10% output reduction commitment. We urge member enterprises to translate planned maintenance into measurable output outcomes and to strengthen industry self-regulation, ensuring smelting capacity discipline and healthy development of the industrial chain. Relevant departments will continue monitoring industry operation and coordination.

We acknowledge the Government's statement and share the principle that any restart requires an agreed legal framework and fiscal terms. From our side: Cobre Panama remains on care and maintenance, we continue incurring significant preservation costs with no timeline announced, and we remain ready to engage in constructive dialogue whenever the Government determines the process. We make no assumptions on 2027 volumes and encourage all parties to await the jointly determined framework.

We look forward to constructive discussions with our long-standing Chinese partners during Asia Copper Week, 17–19 November. We note that market participants already have transparent daily references, including the SMM imported concentrate index, and our own provisional mid-2026 settlements moved to index-linked terms. We will not comment on any negotiation outcomes in advance.

We note the QB revision. Mine supply increments are indeed facing operational and structural constraints — Chilean ore grades have fallen 13% in four years — but underperformance at individual assets does not negate the aggregate response: Codelco's multi-year investment program is being executed to reverse our output trajectory, consistent with Cochilco's forecast of +5.2% Chilean production growth in 2027.

Following Asia Copper Week discussions, NDRC and MIIT reiterate support for the smelting sector's self-discipline efforts, note the verification of Q4 maintenance programs, and encourage both Chinese smelters and international miners to conclude 2027 benchmark terms in a spirit of mutual benefit that safeguards the security and stability of the industrial chain and supply chain. Decisions on the sulphuric acid export policy due for review around January 2027 will be announced in due course following assessment of market conditions.

Antofagasta confirms that discussions regarding 2027 benchmark terms with its Chinese customers concluded during Asia Copper Week in Shanghai. We thank our counterparts for their constructive engagement. In accordance with our practice and as jointly agreed, we will not comment on the terms discussed; any disclosure will be made only by mutual consent of the parties.

To support a constructive path forward, First Quantum is prepared to discuss an expanded fiscal package for any restart of Cobre Panama — including increased royalty participation and an upfront contribution toward an independently administered fund for an orderly, phased closure. These proposals are offered without prejudice; the scope, timing and legal structure of any restart remain subject to approval by the Government of Panama.

twitter.content: CSPT confirms participation in 2027 benchmark talks during Asia Copper Week. We cannot accept index linkage to a spot index trading at −$231.68/dmt — that institutionalizes unviability for custom smelters. We propose instead: a fixed 2027 benchmark TC at no less than $0/t with an upward floor mechanism tied to verified concentrate supply growth, long-term volume guarantees for Jiangxi Copper, Tongling and CSPT members, and quarterly review clauses.

The Government of Panama, acting on the commission's 30 September 2026 recommendation, agrees to convene bilateral technical working groups with First Quantum Minerals. Any process proceeds under Panamanian law and sovereignty: talks are exploratory, entail no commitment to restart, and the funded orderly-closure mechanism will be addressed in parallel with — not subordinated to — restart discussions. All outcomes remain subject to environmental review and approval by the competent national authorities.

Ivanhoe Mines provides a Phase 4 update: the definitive feasibility study for the replicate 6 Mtpa concentrator is progressing, with the study and long-term mine plan on track for publication. Phase 4 remains on schedule to begin contributing approximately 500,000 tonnes per year of additional production from 2028, and is not included in our 2026 guidance of 380,000–420,000 t or 2027 guidance of 500,000–540,000 t. Steady progress, on track.

Codelco publishes its multi-year investment plan progress update ahead of schedule: structural projects at El Teniente (New Mine Level) and Chuquicamata (underground ramp-up) remain in execution, with 2026 milestones largely met despite the structural decline in ore grades (-13% in Chile over four years). We reaffirm our contribution to the projected recovery of Chilean output in 2027, consistent with Cochilco's +5.2% forecast. Safety remains our first priority; operational discipline and long-term reliability for our customers guide every decision.

First Quantum Minerals welcomes the Government of Panama's decision to convene bilateral technical working groups. We can confirm participation and note that our teams have maintained Cobre Panama in care and maintenance, preserving operational readiness that supports an orderly, phased restart under any framework approved by Panamanian authorities. We approach these exploratory talks in good faith and will not prejudge outcomes, respecting Panama's legal and environmental processes throughout.

We note CSPT's stated position ahead of Asia Copper Week. As always, we will not comment on the substance of ongoing discussions, but we look forward to constructive dialogue with our long-standing Chinese customers. We would simply observe that market participants should reflect on where concentrate supply-demand balances and the SMM imported concentrate index currently sit — and that any durable 2027 outcome must remain grounded in verified market fundamentals.

twitter.content: We take note of the concluded 2027 benchmark discussions. We will monitor Q4 maintenance execution and concentrate utilization against the CSPT commitment, and reserve the right to apply capacity-replacement, raw-material inspection and resource-utilization measures to enterprises whose conduct undermines industry self-discipline.

While 2027 benchmark terms remain confidential, we note that deeply negative spot treatment charges reflect a concentrate market under real physical strain. As Chile's state producer, Codelco's response is structural: our multi-year investment plan targets renewed output consistent with Chile's projected +5.2% recovery in 2027, prioritizing long-term reliable supply over short-cycle positioning.

First Quantum Minerals accepts the Government of Panama's terms for bilateral technical working groups, including the two parallel tracks, independent environmental verification and full transparency on care-and-maintenance status. We confirm readiness to begin talks within the 60-day window and reiterate that any restart remains subject to approval by the Government of Panama under Panamanian law.

We call on the industry to continue implementing capacity discipline and capacity-replacement requirements so that byproduct markets support, not substitute for, structural adjustment.

twitter.content: CSPT welcomes NDRC/MIIT's continued support for sector self-discipline. First Quantum Minerals confirms delivery of the agreed documentation to the bilateral technical working groups: complete care-and-maintenance records, environmental compliance reports and tailings management safeguards for independent verification, covering the period since November 2023. Qualified enterprises may apply under enhanced customs and tax supervision to ensure orderly trade and comprehensive resource utilization. We remind the industry that byproduct market normalization supports—not substitutes for—capacity discipline and capacity-replacement requirements.

Antofagasta remains committed to concluding 2027 benchmark terms with its Chinese partners by end-Q1. We remain open to concluding 2027–2029 reciprocal volume commitments by 31 March 2027 and look forward to continued discussions.

Codelco confirms its multi-year structural projects at El Teniente and Chuquicamata remain on schedule, consistent with our output-recovery plan and Cochilco's projection of a +5.2% rebound in Chilean production in 2027. As we stated in February, our 2027 concentrate allocations to longstanding customers will be honored in full; we will not comment on ongoing benchmark negotiations, which we trust will conclude constructively by end-Q1.

First Quantum Minerals accepts the Government of Panama's proposal to continue the bilateral technical working groups on the stated basis, including the orderly-closure funding track. We view this as a constructive framework consistent with our shared objective of a lawful, phased path forward for Cobre Panama, and confirm our continued participation without preconditions.

Antofagasta plc is pleased to confirm agreement with its Chinese partners on 2027 benchmark treatment charge and refining charge terms: quarterly linkage to the SMM imported concentrate index with a $0/t floor and a +$40/t cap above index, quarterly review, settlement effective 31 March 2027. We believe this transparent, index-referenced architecture serves long-term supply security for our customers and preserves market-based price discovery. No further details of commercial terms will be disclosed.

We look forward to concluding terms with our customers before 31 March 2027.

The Government of Panama: We welcome confirmation that independent verification will now commence, and we reaffirm full cooperation with the technical working groups. As agreed, Cobre Panama remains in care and maintenance; any restart remains conditional on the legal framework determined by the Government of Panama, and no scope or timeline is presumed on our part.

We encourage convergence on quarterly index-linkage with an asymmetric collar as a workable market-based arrangement, and take note of the Q1 output discipline pledge. We remind all parties that sustained discipline will be assessed against delivered volumes, given that 2026 refined output grew ~4% despite the November 2025 pledge; reciprocal re-openers are essential to keep long-term contracts consistent with orderly supply.

Codelco welcomes CSPT's move toward index linkage with a shared collar as a pragmatic step toward transparent risk-sharing; as a major concentrate seller, we note that asymmetric floors and caps inevitably steer tonnage toward whoever bids above index. Our 2027 shipments remain committed under existing contract structures; we encourage settlement by 31 March so planning certainty prevails for both smelters and miners.
